const char *language_registry(void){ return g_lang->reg; }
/* The language played, as NFSU2_LANGUAGE names it ("english" ... "portuguese") */
const char *language_name(void){ return g_lang->key; }

/* The game's text for a hash in the language it plays in: 0x4ff9d0's binary
 * search over the loaded strings ([0x8383d8]: { hash, text } sorted by hash,
 * [0x8383d0] of them).  0 before a language is loaded, or for a hash it lacks. */
static uint32_t game_text(uint32_t hash){
    uint32_t tab = MR32(0x8383d8u), n = MR32(0x8383d0u);
    if (!tab || !n || n > 0x100000u || !mem_is_committed(tab) || !mem_is_committed(tab + 8u*n - 1u)) return 0;
    uint32_t lo = 0, hi = n;
    while (lo < hi){
        uint32_t mid = lo + (hi - lo) / 2, h = MR32(tab + 8u*mid);
        if (h == hash) return MR32(tab + 8u*mid + 4u);
        if (h < hash) lo = mid + 1; else hi = mid;
    }
    return 0;
}
uint32_t language_text(uint32_t hash){ return game_text(hash); }
/* Whether a profile name (16 bytes at most) is the game's "No Profile": what
 * 0x512360 puts in the profile's name (0x83a9e0) while none is loaded, in the
 * game's language ("Aucun profil", "Kein Profil", ...). */
int language_no_profile(const char *name){
    if (!strcasecmp(name, "No Profile")) return 1;
    uint32_t s = game_text(0xcf4f80c2u);
    if (!s) s = game_text(0xc01a6f63u);
    return s && mem_is_committed(s) && mem_is_committed(s + 15u) && !strncasecmp(name, (const char *)(g_mem + s), 16);
}

/* ---- texts of our own --------------------------------------------------------
 * Texts the game shows but has none of (the free-roam race questions' buttons,
 * roam_game.c; our SMS, sms.c) go into its language table under names of ours,
 * so that it looks them up as its own.  The table is a sorted {hash, char*}
 * array that the game only points into its language chunk (0x5125B0 loads it,
 * 0x4FFAE0 clears it).  Each frame (the main-loop hook) a table that is not
 * ours, or one older than a text added since, is replaced by a copy with every
 * text of ours merged in by hash (unsigned, as 0x4FF9D0 compares; a hash the
 * game has keeps the game's), their strings after the entries.  The game's own
 * array stays as it was, for the next copy. */
void dispatch_indirect(CPU *c, uint32_t addr);
#define G_LANG      0x008383d8u
#define G_LANG_N    0x008383d0u
#define OWN_MAX     64         /* roam_game.c 4, sms.c 5, mpcredit.c 2, photo.c 1, vinylcat.c 1, modpacks.c a rim brand's each */
static struct { uint32_t hash; char text[1024]; } g_own[OWN_MAX];
static int g_nown, g_own_merged;            /* texts named; how many of them the copy has */
static uint32_t g_own_copy, g_own_from, g_own_from_n;   /* the copy, while the game points at it; the game's array */

uint32_t language_add_text(const char *name, const char *text){
    uint32_t h = 0xffffffffu;                   /* bStringHash (0x43DB50) */
    for (const char *s = name; *s; s++) h = h * 33u + (uint8_t)*s;
    int i = 0;
    while (i < g_nown && g_own[i].hash != h) i++;
    if (i == OWN_MAX){ fprintf(stderr, "language: no room for the text %s\n", name); return h; }
    if (i == g_nown) g_nown++;
    g_own[i].hash = h;
    snprintf(g_own[i].text, sizeof g_own[i].text, "%s", text);
    g_own_merged = -1;                          /* a new copy, also for a text changed */
    return h;
}

/* operator new in guest memory, from the main-loop hook */
static uint32_t guest_new(CPU *c, uint32_t size){
    CPU save = *c;
    c->esp = (c->esp - 256u) & ~15u;
    PUSH32(size);
    PUSH32(GUEST_RET_MAINLOOP);                        /* the hook's return address: the callee's ret pops it */
    dispatch_indirect(c, FN_NEW);
    uint32_t r = c->eax;
    *c = save;
    return r;
}

void language_texts_frame(CPU *c){
    uint32_t t = MR32(G_LANG), n = MR32(G_LANG_N);
    if (!g_nown || !t || !n || n > 0x100000u) return;
    if (t == g_own_copy){
        if (g_own_merged == g_nown) return;
        t = g_own_from; n = g_own_from_n;
    }
    if (!mem_is_committed(t) || !mem_is_committed(t + 8u*n - 1u)) return;
    int ord[OWN_MAX];
    uint32_t strs = 0;
    for (int i = 0; i < g_nown; i++){ ord[i] = i; strs += (uint32_t)strlen(g_own[i].text) + 1u; }
    for (int i = 1; i < g_nown; i++)
        for (int j = i; j > 0 && g_own[ord[j - 1]].hash > g_own[ord[j]].hash; j--){ int x = ord[j]; ord[j] = ord[j - 1]; ord[j - 1] = x; }
    uint32_t mem = guest_new(c, (n + (uint32_t)g_nown) * 8u + strs);
    if (!mem){ fprintf(stderr, "language: guest memory for our texts failed\n"); g_own_copy = t; g_own_merged = g_nown; return; }
    uint32_t sp = mem + (n + (uint32_t)g_nown) * 8u, sa[OWN_MAX];
    for (int i = 0; i < g_nown; i++){
        size_t l = strlen(g_own[i].text) + 1u;
        memcpy(g_mem + sp, g_own[i].text, l); sa[i] = sp; sp += (uint32_t)l;
    }
    uint32_t o = 0; int k = 0, kept = 0;
    for (uint32_t i = 0; i <= n; i++){
        uint32_t h = i < n ? MR32(t + 8u*i) : 0xffffffffu;
        while (k < g_nown && g_own[ord[k]].hash <= h){
            if (g_own[ord[k]].hash == h && i < n){ k++; kept++; continue; }   /* the game has the name already */
            MR32(mem + 8u*o) = g_own[ord[k]].hash; MR32(mem + 8u*o + 4u) = sa[ord[k]]; o++; k++;
        }
        if (i < n){ MR32(mem + 8u*o) = h; MR32(mem + 8u*o + 4u) = MR32(t + 8u*i + 4u); o++; }
    }
    MR32(G_LANG) = mem; MR32(G_LANG_N) = o;
    g_own_copy = mem; g_own_from = t; g_own_from_n = n; g_own_merged = g_nown;
    fprintf(stderr, "language: %d text%s of our own added to the game's %u%s\n", g_nown - kept, g_nown - kept == 1 ? "" : "s", n,
            kept ? " (some names the game has already: the game's stay)" : "");
}

/* A text of ours (UTF-8) in the game's letters: Latin-1, as its language files
 * write theirs; Polish's letters as its pack's fonts draw them (e-ogonek
 * 0xBF, l-stroke 0xEE, s-acute 0xE2 ...; hornmenu.c), Turkish's too (dotless
 * i 0xED, s-cedilla 0xFF, g-breve 0xFD ...; its English.bin's), Hungarian's
 * o and u with the double acute as its text has them (o-tilde 0xF5,
 * u-circumflex 0xFB), Czech's letters with the caron and u with the ring
 * without them (c, r, s, u ...), Slovak's in Windows-1250 as its pack's fonts
 * draw them, Greek's as greek_byte puts them; a letter the fonts lack as '?'.
 * Korean, Chinese, Japanese, Thai, Russian and Ukrainian draw ASCII as it is
 * (car names), not Latin-1's accented letters. */
/* Greek's letters in its pack (tools/greekfont/build_greek.py: GREEK, SLOTS,
 * PUNCT, PRESERVE): the 69 of monotonic Greek in Unicode's order (Ά, Έ Ή Ί, Ό,
 * Ύ to Ρ, Σ to ώ) on bytes 0xA1 up, past the Latin-1 letters it keeps (NBSP,
 * © « ® · » ¼ Ñ, as they are); the quotes, … and ™ on the English file's own
 * bytes for them; '?' for any other */
static uint8_t greek_byte(uint32_t u){
    static const uint8_t KEEP[] = { 0xa0, 0xa9, 0xab, 0xae, 0xb7, 0xbb, 0xbc, 0xd1 };
    for (unsigned i = 0; i < sizeof KEEP; i++) if (u == KEEP[i]) return (uint8_t)u;
    if (u == 0x201c) return 0x87;
    if (u == 0x201d) return 0x84;
    if (u == 0x2026) return 0x86;
    if (u == 0x2122) return 0x82;
    int k = u == 0x386 ? 0 : u >= 0x388 && u <= 0x38a ? 1 + (int)(u - 0x388) : u == 0x38c ? 4
          : u >= 0x38e && u <= 0x3a1 ? 5 + (int)(u - 0x38e) : u >= 0x3a3 && u <= 0x3ce ? 25 + (int)(u - 0x3a3) : -1;
    if (k < 0) return '?';
    for (unsigned b = 0xa1; b < 0x100; b++){
        int kept = 0;
        for (unsigned i = 0; i < sizeof KEEP; i++) kept |= b == KEEP[i];
        if (!kept && k-- == 0) return (uint8_t)b;
    }
    return '?';
}
void language_game_letters(const char *utf8, char *out, size_t n){
    static const struct { uint16_t u; uint8_t b; } PL[] = {
        { 0x105, 0xe7 }, { 0x107, 0xe9 }, { 0x119, 0xbf }, { 0x142, 0xee }, { 0x144, 0xf1 }, { 0xf3, 0xf3 },
        { 0x15b, 0xe2 }, { 0x17a, 0xeb }, { 0x17c, 0xe1 }, { 0x104, 0xfd }, { 0x106, 0xc8 }, { 0x118, 0xc7 },
        { 0x141, 0xfa }, { 0x143, 0xd1 }, { 0xd3, 0xd3 }, { 0x15a, 0xda }, { 0x17b, 0xc9 },
    }, TR[] = {
        { 0x131, 0xed }, { 0x130, 0xcd }, { 0x15f, 0xff }, { 0x15e, 0xfe }, { 0x11f, 0xfd }, { 0x11e, 0xdd },
    }, HU[] = {
        { 0x151, 0xf5 }, { 0x150, 0xd5 }, { 0x171, 0xfb }, { 0x170, 0xdb },
    }, CS[] = {
        { 0x10d, 'c' }, { 0x10c, 'C' }, { 0x10f, 'd' }, { 0x10e, 'D' }, { 0x11b, 'e' }, { 0x11a, 'E' },
        { 0x148, 'n' }, { 0x147, 'N' }, { 0x159, 'r' }, { 0x158, 'R' }, { 0x161, 's' }, { 0x160, 'S' },
        { 0x165, 't' }, { 0x164, 'T' }, { 0x16f, 'u' }, { 0x16e, 'U' }, { 0x17e, 'z' }, { 0x17d, 'Z' },
    }, SK[] = {
        { 0xe1, 0xe1 }, { 0xe4, 0xe4 }, { 0x10d, 0xe8 }, { 0x10f, 0xef }, { 0xe9, 0xe9 }, { 0xed, 0xed },
        { 0x13a, 0xe5 }, { 0x13e, 0xbe }, { 0x148, 0xf2 }, { 0xf3, 0xf3 }, { 0xf4, 0xf4 }, { 0x155, 0xe0 },
        { 0x161, 0x9a }, { 0x165, 0x9d }, { 0xfa, 0xfa }, { 0xfd, 0xfd }, { 0x17e, 0x9e },
        { 0xc1, 0xc1 }, { 0xc4, 0xc4 }, { 0x10c, 0xc8 }, { 0x10e, 0xcf }, { 0xc9, 0xc9 }, { 0xcd, 0xcd },
        { 0x139, 0xc5 }, { 0x13d, 0xbc }, { 0x147, 0xd2 }, { 0xd3, 0xd3 }, { 0xd4, 0xd4 }, { 0x154, 0xc0 },
        { 0x160, 0x8a }, { 0x164, 0x8d }, { 0xda, 0xda }, { 0xdd, 0xdd }, { 0x17d, 0x8e },
    };
    int polish = !strcmp(g_lang->key, "polish"), turkish = !strcmp(g_lang->key, "turkish");
    int hungarian = !strcmp(g_lang->key, "hungarian"), czech = !strcmp(g_lang->key, "czech"), slovak = !strcmp(g_lang->key, "slovak");
    int greek = !strcmp(g_lang->key, "greek");
    int latin = !g_lang->fonts && strcmp(g_lang->key, "russian") && strcmp(g_lang->key, "ukrainian") && !slovak && !greek;
    const uint8_t *s = (const uint8_t *)utf8;
    size_t o = 0;
    while (*s && o + 1 < n){
        uint32_t u = *s++;
        if (u >= 0xc0){
            int more = u >= 0xf0 ? 3 : u >= 0xe0 ? 2 : 1;
            u &= 0x3fu >> more;
            while (more-- && (*s & 0xc0) == 0x80) u = u << 6 | (*s++ & 0x3fu);
        }
        uint8_t b = '?';
        if (u < 0x80) b = (uint8_t)u;
        else if (u == 0x2019 || u == 0x2018) b = '\'';
        else if (u == 0x2013 || u == 0x2014) b = '-';
        else if (polish){ for (unsigned i = 0; i < sizeof PL / sizeof PL[0]; i++) if (PL[i].u == u) b = PL[i].b; }
        else if (turkish && u >= 0x100){ for (unsigned i = 0; i < sizeof TR / sizeof TR[0]; i++) if (TR[i].u == u) b = TR[i].b; }
        else if (hungarian && u >= 0x100){ for (unsigned i = 0; i < sizeof HU / sizeof HU[0]; i++) if (HU[i].u == u) b = HU[i].b; }
        else if (czech && u >= 0x100){ for (unsigned i = 0; i < sizeof CS / sizeof CS[0]; i++) if (CS[i].u == u) b = CS[i].b; }
        else if (slovak){ for (unsigned i = 0; i < sizeof SK / sizeof SK[0]; i++) if (SK[i].u == u) b = SK[i].b; }
        else if (greek) b = greek_byte(u);
        else if (latin && u >= 0xa0 && u < 0x100) b = (uint8_t)u;
        out[o++] = (char)b;
    }
    out[o] = 0;
}

/* The subtitles' check, 0x50d350 (the front end's movies and InGamePlayMovie's
 * next one) and its copy in InGamePlayMovie's constructor: the last of its
 * region tests, "region == 12", made true for a language whose text has the
 * movies' lines (the PSA's first, "Hi, I'm Brooke Burke"), English only with
 * its pack. */
int language_hook(CPU *c, uint32_t ip){
    switch (ip){
    case HOOK_SITE(0x0050d388):           /* cmp eax, 0xc; sete al */
    case HOOK_SITE(0x00553a62): {         /* cmp eax, 0xc; jne (no subtitles) */
        uint32_t s = g_subtitles && (g_lang != &LANGS[0] || g_english_pack) ? game_text(0x03812413u) : 0;
        if (s && mem_is_committed(s) && MR8(s)) c->eax = 0xc;
        return 1; }
    }
    return 0;
}

/* what a font block's hashes add up to in the size table (0x4ff680's sum) */
static uint32_t fonts_total(uint32_t block){
    uint32_t t = 0;
    for (uint32_t h; (h = MR32(block)) != 0; block += 4)
        for (uint32_t i = 0; i < 15; i++)
            if (MR32(FONT_SIZES + 8*i) == h && (int32_t)MR32(FONT_SIZES + 8*i + 4) > 0) t += MR32(FONT_SIZES + 8*i + 4);
    return t;
}

void language_install(void){
    const char *e = getenv("NFSU2_LANGUAGE");
    if (e && *e){
        size_t i, n = sizeof LANGS / sizeof LANGS[0];
        for (i = 0; i < n && strcasecmp(e, LANGS[i].key); i++) {}
        if (i < n) g_lang = &LANGS[i];
        else fprintf(stderr, "language: \"%s\" is not one of the game's, English it is\n", e);
    }
    const char *v = getenv("NFSU2_SUBTITLES");
    if (v && (v[0] == '0' || !strcasecmp(v, "off") || !strcasecmp(v, "no"))) g_subtitles = 0;

    char pack[64]; snprintf(pack, sizeof pack, "LANGPACKS/%s", g_lang->key);
    int files = fileio_set_language_pack(pack);
    if (g_lang == &LANGS[0]){
        g_english_pack = files > 0;
        if (files) fprintf(stderr, "language: english, %s: the movies' subtitles%s\n", pack, g_subtitles ? "" : " (off)");
        return;
    }
    fprintf(stderr, "language: %s (registry \"%s\"), %s: %d file%s\n", g_lang->key, g_lang->reg,
            pack, files, files == 1 ? "" : "s");
    /* Greek's pack adds its letters' glyph records to the fonts (each letter twice: its byte and its Unicode):
     * the language pool 64 KB more, as a font block's size in the table does */
    if (!strcmp(g_lang->key, "greek") && files){
        if (MR32(FONT_SIZES) == MR32(LATIN_FONTS) && MR32(FONT_SIZES + 4) == 0){
            MR32(FONT_SIZES + 4) = 65536u;
            fprintf(stderr, "language: the language pool 64 KB more for Greek's letters\n");
        } else fprintf(stderr, "language: the exe's font table is not the one expected, Greek's pool left as it is\n");
    }
    if (!g_lang->fonts) return;

    /* only on the data of the exe this port is made for */
    if (MR32(FONT_SIZES) != MR32(LATIN_FONTS) || MR32(FONT_SIZES + 4) != 0
        || MR32(JA_ENTRY) != 10 || MR32(JA_ENTRY + 4) != JA_NAME || MR32(JA_ENTRY + 8) != JA_FILE
        || MR32(JA_ENTRY + 12) != JA_FONTS || MR32(JA_FONTS + 16) != 0
        || memcmp(g_mem + JA_NAME, "JAPANESE", 9) || memcmp(g_mem + JA_FILE, "LANGUAGES\\JAPANESE.BIN", 23)){
        fprintf(stderr, "language: the exe's language table is not the one expected, left as it is\n");
        return;
    }
    if (g_lang->thai){
        MR32(JA_ENTRY) = 11;
        memcpy(g_mem + JA_NAME, "THAILAND", 8);
        memcpy(g_mem + JA_FILE + 10, "THAILAND", 8);
        for (int i = 0; i < 4; i++) MR32(JA_FONTS + 4u*i) = THAI_FONTS[i];
    }
    uint32_t need = fonts_total(g_lang->fonts), have = fonts_total(LATIN_FONTS);
    if (need > have){
        MR32(FONT_SIZES + 4) = need - have;
        fprintf(stderr, "language: the language pool is sized for its fonts (%u KB, not %u)\n", need >> 10, have >> 10);
    }
}

/* lifecycle.c -- quitting and app activation, delivered the way Windows does.
 *
 * Quit (Cmd-Q, the window's close button, Dock > Quit, logout):
 *   the request becomes a WM_CLOSE in the guest's message queue, like the
 *   close box / Alt-F4 on Windows.  The game's WndProc (0x5CCD60) sets its
 *   quit flag [0x864F4C] -- except while PC_Loading.fng is up (0x4A9330),
 *   so the message is re-posted every second -- its main loop (0x5811C0)
 *   returns and the game shuts down through its own code to ExitProcess.
 *   Only then does the host leave its event loop.  A second request, or
 *   NFSU2_QUIT_GRACE seconds (default 10) without the guest exiting, forces
 *   the exit.  Either way main() then waits for save files the game still
 *   has open for writing (lifecycle_drain_writes) and freezes the guest
 *   threads before the process exits, so no save is cut in half.
 *
 * Activation (Cmd-Tab, clicking another app, hiding the app):
 *   deactivation sends WM_ACTIVATE(WA_INACTIVE), WM_ACTIVATEAPP(FALSE),
 *   WM_KILLFOCUS; activation WM_ACTIVATEAPP(TRUE), WM_ACTIVATE(WA_ACTIVE),
 *   WM_SETFOCUS (the order Windows uses).  WM_ACTIVATE pauses / resumes the
 *   game's own sound (EAXSound [0x82B884]: 0x4810F0 / 0x481210) and
 *   WM_ACTIVATEAPP(FALSE) clears [0x870988], after which the pump (0x5BF1C0)
 *   blocks in GetMessageA until the app is active again: the game freezes in
 *   the background exactly as it does after an alt-tab on Windows.
 *   NFSU2_BACKGROUND=run keeps it running instead (no messages are sent).
 *   During a LAN session the game is not parked (lifecycle_may_park): the
 *   messages still go out, but it keeps running, as the game itself does in
 *   a network race.
 *
 * The host side (AppKit main thread) only flips atomics; everything that
 * touches the guest message queue runs on the guest thread, in
 * PeekMessageA/GetMessageA (lifecycle_pump), so the queue stays
 * single-threaded. */
#include <stdio.h>
#include <stdlib.h>
#include <string.h>
#include <strings.h>
#include <stdint.h>
#include <stdatomic.h>
#include <time.h>
#include <unistd.h>

void win32_post_message(uint32_t m, uint32_t wp, uint32_t lp);   /* win32_ext.c */
void metal_request_quit(void);                                     /* metal.m */
int  fileio_open_writers(void);                                    /* fileio.c */

#define WM_ACTIVATE    0x0006u
#define WM_SETFOCUS    0x0007u
#define WM_KILLFOCUS   0x0008u
#define WM_CLOSE       0x0010u
#define WM_ACTIVATEAPP 0x001Cu

static double mono_s(void){
    struct timespec ts; clock_gettime(CLOCK_MONOTONIC, &ts);
    return (double)ts.tv_sec + ts.tv_nsec / 1e9;
}

/* ---- quit ---------------------------------------------------------------- */
static _Atomic int    g_quit_req = 0;        /* requests so far (Cmd-Q, close...) */
static _Atomic int    g_guest_gone = 0;      /* guest called ExitProcess / returned */
static _Atomic int    g_leaving = 0;         /* host loop told to stop */
static _Atomic double g_quit_t0 = 0;         /* time of the first request */
static double         g_close_last = 0;
static int            g_close_sent = 0;

static double quit_grace_s(void){
    const char *e = getenv("NFSU2_QUIT_GRACE");
    double g = (e && *e) ? atof(e) : 10.0;
    return g > 0 ? g : 10.0;
}
static void leave(const char *why){
    if (atomic_exchange(&g_leaving, 1)) return;
    fprintf(stderr, "app: leaving the event loop (%s)\n", why);
    metal_request_quit();
}

/* Host thread: Cmd-Q, window close, Dock > Quit; guest thread: autotest
 * "close".  The time is stored before the request is counted, so
 * lifecycle_tick never sees a request without its start time. */
void lifecycle_request_quit(const char *why){
    double none = 0;
    atomic_compare_exchange_strong(&g_quit_t0, &none, mono_s());
    int n = atomic_fetch_add(&g_quit_req, 1) + 1;
    if (n == 1){
        fprintf(stderr, "app: quit requested (%s) -> WM_CLOSE to the game\n", why);
    } else if (n == 2){
        fprintf(stderr, "app: quit requested again (%s) -> forcing the exit\n", why);
        leave("second quit request");
    }
    if (atomic_load(&g_guest_gone)) leave("guest already exited");
}
int lifecycle_quit_requested(void){ return atomic_load(&g_quit_req) > 0; }

/* boot.c, when the guest's entry point returns or calls ExitProcess. */
void lifecycle_guest_exited(int code){
    atomic_store(&g_guest_gone, 1);
    fprintf(stderr, "app: the game exited (code %d)%s\n", code,
            atomic_load(&g_quit_req) ? " after the quit request" : "");
    if (getenv("WINDOW")) leave("game exited");
}

/* Host event loop, once per iteration: enforces the grace period. */
void lifecycle_tick(void){
    if (!atomic_load(&g_quit_req) || atomic_load(&g_leaving)) return;
    if (mono_s() - atomic_load(&g_quit_t0) > quit_grace_s()){
        fprintf(stderr, "app: the game did not exit within %g s of WM_CLOSE\n", quit_grace_s());
        leave("quit grace period over");
    }
}

/* main(), after the event loop: give the game time to finish writing and
 * close its save files (the guest threads still run).  Returns the number
 * of write handles still open when it gave up. */
int lifecycle_drain_writes(double max_s){
    double t0 = mono_s();
    int n = fileio_open_writers();
    if (n) fprintf(stderr, "app: waiting for %d open save file(s) to be closed\n", n);
    while (n && mono_s() - t0 < max_s){
        usleep(10000);
        n = fileio_open_writers();
    }
    if (n) fprintf(stderr, "app: %d file(s) still open for writing after %.1f s\n", n, max_s);
    return n;
}

/* ---- activation ----------------------------------------------------------- */
static _Atomic int g_want_active = 1;        /* what AppKit says */
static int         g_told_active = 1;        /* what the game was told (guest thread) */
static _Atomic int64_t g_blur_until_ms = 0;  /* autotest "blur": re-activate at this time (monotonic ms:
                                              * 64-bit, the browser clock is epoch-based) */
static int g_bg_mode = -1;                   /* 1 = NFSU2_BACKGROUND=run */

static int background_runs(void){
    if (g_bg_mode < 0){
        const char *e = getenv("NFSU2_BACKGROUND");
        g_bg_mode = (e && (!strcasecmp(e, "run") || !strcasecmp(e, "1") || !strcasecmp(e, "on"))) ? 1 : 0;
    }
    return g_bg_mode;
}
double audio_time(void);                                           /* audio.m */
void discord_lifecycle_changed(void);                              /* discord.c */
void roam_game_parked(int on);                                     /* roam_game.c: friends see "paused" */
static void set_active(int on, const char *why){
    if (atomic_exchange(&g_want_active, on ? 1 : 0) != (on ? 1 : 0))
        fprintf(stderr, "app: %s (%s, audio t=%.3f s)\n", on ? "activated" : "deactivated",
                why, audio_time());
}
/* Host thread: NSApplicationDidBecomeActive / DidResignActive.  Ignored for
 * NOFOCUS test runs: their window is never meant to be the active one. */
void lifecycle_set_active(int on, const char *why){
    const char *nf = getenv("NOFOCUS");
    if (background_runs() || (nf && *nf && *nf != '0')) return;
    set_active(on, why);
}
/* autotest "blur MS": deactivate now, re-activate MS ms later (the guest is
 * frozen meanwhile, so the script cannot do it itself).  With background =
 * run the game is never told, as on the real path above, so a test can tell
 * pause from run. */
void lifecycle_simulate_blur(long ms){
    if (background_runs()){
        fprintf(stderr, "app: autotest blur ignored: background = run keeps the game going\n");
        return;
    }
    atomic_store(&g_blur_until_ms, (int64_t)(mono_s() * 1000.0) + ms);
    set_active(0, "autotest blur");
}

/* win32_ext.c GetMessageA: may the inactive game be parked there?  The game
 * never parks in a network race: its pump (0x5BF1C0) only peeks while
 * World::IsOnline (0x5F00F0: [0x89CF69], [0x8669F4] > 0 or [0x866A14] > 0).
 * In the LAN screens, the lobby and the game room it does, and a parked game
 * stops answering its lobby server's ping (server.cfg PINGWAIT 30 s): the
 * server drops it, and a host's own drop ends every player's session.  Mac
 * players switch apps often, so while a LAN session is open (from the
 * game's WSAStartup on its LAN screens to the last WSACleanup) the game is
 * not parked: the deactivation messages still went out (the game paused its
 * sound and ignores input, [0x870988] = 0), it just keeps running as in a
 * network race, with the output muted as when parked.  Single-player is
 * unchanged. */
int winsock_session_active(void);                                  /* winsock.c */
void audio_set_muted(int on);                                      /* audio.m */
static int g_inactive_gen, g_park_noted = -1, g_session_muted;
int lifecycle_may_park(void){
    if (g_told_active) return 0;
    if (winsock_session_active()){
        if (g_park_noted != g_inactive_gen){
            g_park_noted = g_inactive_gen;
            fprintf(stderr, "app: in the background during a LAN session: the game keeps running (sound paused) "
                    "so the other players do not drop it\n");
            audio_set_muted(1); g_session_muted = 1;
        }
        return 0;
    }
    return 1;
}
/* Parked in the background right now (inactive and outside a LAN session):
 * for code that pauses its own work while the game is parked, the stall
 * watchdog (no report: no frames on purpose) and the Discord status
 * ("Paused").  During a LAN session in the background the game keeps
 * running, so neither treats it as parked. */
int lifecycle_game_parked(void){ return !g_told_active && !winsock_session_active(); }
/* Passes lifecycle_game_parked() on when it changes: the Discord status
 * ("Paused") and free-roam friends (roam_game.c: "paused") follow the
 * parked state, not the activation, so a game kept running in a LAN session
 * in the background is not announced as paused, and a LAN session that ends
 * while the app is in the background parks it (and announces it) then.
 * Guest thread, once per pump. */
static int g_parked_told;
static void parked_pump(void){
    int p = lifecycle_game_parked();
    if (p == g_parked_told) return;
    g_parked_told = p;
    discord_lifecycle_changed();                  /* presence: paused while parked */
    roam_game_parked(p);                          /* free-roam friends: paused while parked */
}

/* Guest thread, from PeekMessageA/GetMessageA once the game window exists:
 * turns pending host events into window messages. */
void lifecycle_pump(void){
    int64_t bu = atomic_load(&g_blur_until_ms);
    if (bu && (int64_t)(mono_s() * 1000.0) >= bu){
        atomic_store(&g_blur_until_ms, 0);
        set_active(1, "autotest blur over");
    }
    int want = atomic_load(&g_want_active);
    if (want != g_told_active){
        g_told_active = want;
        if (want){
            g_session_muted = 0;
            audio_set_muted(0);                            /* also after a park woken by a message (win32_ext.c) */
            win32_post_message(WM_ACTIVATEAPP, 1u, 0u);
            win32_post_message(WM_ACTIVATE, 1u, 0u);       /* WA_ACTIVE */
            win32_post_message(WM_SETFOCUS, 0u, 0u);
        } else {
            g_inactive_gen++;
            win32_post_message(WM_ACTIVATE, 0u, 0u);       /* WA_INACTIVE */
            win32_post_message(WM_ACTIVATEAPP, 0u, 0u);
            win32_post_message(WM_KILLFOCUS, 0u, 0u);
        }
    }
    parked_pump();
    if (atomic_load(&g_quit_req)){
        double t = mono_s();
        if (!g_close_sent || t - g_close_last >= 1.0){
            if (g_close_sent == 1) fprintf(stderr, "app: WM_CLOSE ignored (loading screen?), re-posting every second\n");
            g_close_sent++; g_close_last = t;
            win32_post_message(WM_CLOSE, 0u, 0u);
        }
    }
}

/* lightkey.c -- the headlights on a key: G tapped turns them off, or back on (the game's own lights, as they were);
 * held (HOLD_S) it is high beam, brighter than the game's own and reaching farther, for as long as it is held, and as
 * they were again when it is let go (off again, if they were off: a flash).  On a controller the right stick straight
 * up does the same (the look's stick: the left one when the game steers with the right one, look.c; none with the
 * look turned off): flicked up and back, on or off; held up, high beam (straight up turns the look by nothing).  Only
 * while the player drives (the drive camera, the HUD on top, the race running: free roam, races, Online and LAN);
 * not paused, in menus, photo mode, a replay or a cutscene.  Friends in free roam see it (roam_game.c: the state's
 * RC_BIT_DARK, its extension's RC_OPEN_HIBEAM), on their screens as on ours.  The key is the player's (the start
 * page's Controls, Site: settings.ini key_lights, NFSU2_KEY_LIGHTS, or off: dinput_kbd.c dikbd_site_key), G by
 * default, the game's "Debug Camera Slow" (nothing without the developers' camera); a player who put one of the
 * game's controls on it (Options, Controls) keeps the key for that: it does nothing here then (dikbd_ours).
 *
 * How the game lights a car (SPEED2.EXE):
 *  - car +0x93D (byte): its headlights are on.  0x5F6190 (from the car's update 0x604740, World::DoTimestep) sets it
 *    each step, 1 but for a flicker of its own (+0x925); 0x604260 sets it 1 at the car's start.  Its readers all
 *    draw: 0x615630 (the flares: the two headlight ones, light hashes 0x9DB90133 and 0xD09091C6, only with it), 0x615490
 *    (each car's headlight glow, 0x60D5D0), 0x60F550 (the light trails' colour: 0 without it).  So "off" is that byte
 *    0 from the main-loop hook on (after the world's step, before the frame is drawn: lightkey_frame), for our car
 *    and each friend's, put back to 1 for a friend's car once its lights are on again (our car's the game's next
 *    step gives back).
 *  - the flares: 0x615630 (thiscall, the car's render info, ret 0x18; its car at +0) takes each light of the car's
 *    list (+0x3F0, the light's hash at +8), its strength (a headlight's 1 + [0x7A6680], 2, capped at 1.0: the
 *    immediate at 0x61594C that ExtraOptions' HighBeamBrightness writes, the same cap for every light) times its
 *    last argument, and draws it with 0x490920 (cdecl: view, light, matrix, strength, ...), which sizes the flare
 *    from the light's least to its most size by the strength, and lights it by it: past 1 bigger and brighter.  High
 *    beam: each headlight flare's strength times K.hi_flare (photo.c's override of 0x615630 names the car,
 *    lightkey_flares; the override of 0x490920 below).
 *  - the road: the player's car's projector (view 9; headlights.c) with HEADLIGHTCOLOR, the colour of the player's
 *    car ([[car +0x554] +0x380], 0x60F510) as the effect constant (ID3DXEffect::SetVector with the handle at +0x574 of
 *    the shader [0x870910] +0x1C, per lit draw: 0x5BDAA0).  d3dx_hle.c's SetVector scales it by
 *    lightkey_road_scale(): 0 off; for high beam headlights.c lights the road from our car once more (a light of the
 *    friends' kind, aimed higher and brighter), the game's own then 0.  Friends' lights (headlights.c) ask
 *    lightkey_state for each car: none when off, brighter and aimed higher on high beam.
 *
 * The game's own look stays as it was while the lights are on.  NFSU2_LIGHTS_LOG=1 logs each press.  Tests: the
 * script command "lights ..." (lightkey_script), tests/web/scripts/lightkey_*.txt, tests/scripts/roam_lights_*.txt. */

 * the view by the stick's angle, so held there the view turns 17 degrees at most */

enum { LK_NORMAL = 0, LK_OFF = 1, LK_HIGH = 2 };

static struct {

    int pst; double pt0;              /* the stick: 0 at rest or elsewhere, 1 up from rest since pt0, 2 not ours till rest */
    int kfl, pfl;                     /* this press of the key, of the stick, has shown high beam: no tap when it ends (a press
                                         is a tap by that, not by when a frame sees it end: at a low frame rate too) */

/* high beam (option D of the rendered variants, the one picked): the flares' strength times hi_flare, the road light times hi_gain and
 * aimed hi_pitch degrees higher (headlights.c) */
static float g_hi_flare = 3.0f, g_hi_gain = 5.0f, g_hi_pitch = 5.0f;

static int lg(void){ static int on = -1; if (on < 0){ const char *e = getenv("NFSU2_LIGHTS_LOG"); on = e && *e == '1'; } return on; }

static uint32_t my_car(void){ uint32_t pl = guest_rd32(G_PLAYER1); return pl ? guest_rd32(pl + PL_CAR) : 0u; }
/* the player drives: the world runs (not paused), the drive camera, the HUD on top, no typing, not photo mode */
static int driving(void){
    uint32_t pl = guest_rd32(G_PLAYER1), r = guest_rd32(G_RACE);
    if (guest_rd32(G_FLOW) != 6u || !guest_ok(pl, PL_MOVER + 4u) || !guest_ok(r, 3) || MR32(r) != 4u || guest_rd32(G_FREEZE)) return 0;
    uint32_t car = guest_rd32(pl + PL_CAR), mv = guest_rd32(pl + PL_MOVER);
    if (!guest_ok(car, 0x9e0) || !guest_ok(mv, MV_TYPE + 4u) || MR32(mv + MV_TYPE) != MOVER_DRIVE) return 0;
    if (mem_is_committed(G_TXT_REC + 3u) && MR8(G_TXT_ON) && MR32(G_TXT_REC)) return 0;
    uint32_t hud = guest_rd32(pl + PL_HUD), fe = guest_rd32(G_FENG), mg = fe ? guest_rd32(fe + 8u) : 0, top = mg ? guest_rd32(mg + 0xe4u) : 0;
    char a[40], b[40];
    guest_read_str(top ? guest_rd32(top + 0xcu) : 0, a, sizeof a); guest_read_str(hud ? guest_rd32(hud + 0x10u) : 0, b, sizeof b);
    return a[0] && !strcasecmp(a, b);
}

/* our lights now: high beam while held, else off when tapped off */
int lightkey_mine(void){
    if (K.test >= 0) return K.test;
    return K.flash ? LK_HIGH : K.off ? LK_OFF : LK_NORMAL;
}
/* a car's lights: ours, a friend's (as its player has them), any other car's as the game has them */
int lightkey_state(uint32_t car){
    if (!car) return LK_NORMAL;
    if (car == K.car) return lightkey_mine();
    for (int k = 0; k < LK_SLOTS; k++) if (K.fcar[k] == car) return K.fst[k];
    return LK_NORMAL;
}
/* roam_game.c, each frame: slot k's car (0: none) and its player's lights */
void lightkey_car(int k, uint32_t car, int st){
    if (k < 0 || k >= LK_SLOTS) return;
    K.fresh = 1;
    if (K.fcar[k] != car){
        /* the slot's car before is gone or another slot's now: never written again from here.  A car new to the slot
         * with its lights off may be one we turned off in another slot: on again below unless its player has them off */
        K.fcar[k] = car; K.fst[k] = LK_NORMAL;
        K.fdark[k] = guest_ok(car, 0x9e0) && !MR8(car + CAR_HL_ON);
    }
    if (!car) return;
    st = st == LK_OFF || st == LK_HIGH ? st : LK_NORMAL;
    if (st != K.fst[k] && lg())
        fprintf(stderr, "[lights] f=%ld slot %d: the friend's lights %s\n", autotest_frame(), k,
                st == LK_OFF ? "off" : st == LK_HIGH ? "on high beam" : "on");
    K.fst[k] = (uint8_t)st;
}

static const char *st_name(int st){ return st == LK_OFF ? "off" : st == LK_HIGH ? "high beam" : "on"; }
static void press_tap(const char *how){
    K.off = !K.off; K.taps++;
    fprintf(stderr, "[lights] f=%ld %s: lights %s\n", autotest_frame(), how, K.off ? "off" : "on");
}

/* the key's presses since the last frame (G unless NFSU2_KEY_LIGHTS; none off): a press let go within HOLD_S turns
 * the lights off or on, one held longer is high beam until it is let go (a tap between two frames counts).  None while
 * the player has one of the game's controls on the key (dikbd_ours: the log says so once) */
static unsigned g_dik = 0x100u;
static void key_input(int can, double t){
    if (g_dik == 0x100u) g_dik = dikbd_site_key("NFSU2_KEY_LIGHTS", DIK_G);
    uint32_t head = kbd_ev_head();
    if (!K.kinit){ K.kinit = 1; K.kseq = head; }
    for (; K.kseq != head; K.kseq++){
        KbdEv e;
        int r = kbd_ev_get(K.kseq, &e);
        if (r == 0) break;
        if (r < 0 || !g_dik || e.dik != g_dik) continue;
        int down = e.down != 0;
        if (down == K.gdown) continue;                                  /* (a repeat) */
        K.gdown = down;
        if (down){
            if (!can || !dikbd_ours(g_dik, "the headlight key")) continue;   /* (the game's control on it: theirs) */
            K.kheld = 1; K.kt0 = t;
        } else if (K.kheld){
            K.kheld = 0;
            if (!K.kfl && can) press_tap(dik_name(g_dik) ? dik_name(g_dik) : "the key");
            K.kfl = 0;
        }
    }
    if (!can){ K.kheld = 0; K.kfl = 0; }
}

/* the look's stick straight up (the right stick; the left one when the game's controls read the right one and none of
 * the left, none when they read both or the player turned the look off: dinput_pad.c pad_look_stick): flicked up and
 * back to rest within HOLD_S, on or off; held up, high beam.  A stick the game steers or brakes with never is (the
 * quick chat's picker keeps the stick from the game, and from here, while it is open) */
int pad_look_stick(void);
static int stick_input(int can, double t){
    PadState s;
    int st = pad_look_stick();
    if (!can || st < 0 || !gamepad_read(&s) || s.wheel){ K.pst = 0; K.pfl = 0; return 0; }
    float x = s.axis[st], y = s.axis[st + 1], r = hypotf(x, y), dir = fabsf(atan2f(x, -y));
    if (!(r == r)) r = 0.f;
    int held = 0;
    if (r < REST_R){
        if (K.pst == 1 && !K.pfl) press_tap(st == PAD_AXIS_LX ? "the left stick up" : "the right stick up");
        K.pst = 0; K.pfl = 0;
    } else if (K.pst == 0){
        if (r >= UP_R) K.pst = dir < UP_RAD ? 1 : 2, K.pt0 = t;           /* up from rest: ours; elsewhere a look */
    } else if (K.pst == 1){
        if (dir > SIDE_RAD){ K.pst = 2; K.pfl = 0; }                  /* turned on to the side: a look round */
        else if ((held = t - K.pt0 >= HOLD_S)) K.pfl = 1;
    }
    return held;
}

static int g_self_lit;              /* headlights.c lit the road from our car this view render (our high beam) */
/* each frame, from the main-loop hook: after the world's step, before the frame is drawn */
void lightkey_frame(CPU *c){
    (void)c;
    double t = now_s();
    int can = driving();
    g_self_lit = 0;                                                     /* (headlights.c says so again as it draws) */
    key_input(can, t);
    int sheld = stick_input(can, t);
    int kheld = K.kheld && t - K.kt0 >= HOLD_S;
    if (kheld) K.kfl = 1;
    int flash = can && (kheld || sheld);
    if (flash && !K.flash){ K.holds++; fprintf(stderr, "[lights] f=%ld %s held: high beam\n", autotest_frame(),
                                       kheld ? (dik_name(g_dik) ? dik_name(g_dik) : "the key") : "the right stick up"); }
    else if (!flash && K.flash) fprintf(stderr, "[lights] f=%ld let go: lights %s\n", autotest_frame(), K.off ? "off" : "on");
    K.flash = flash;
    uint32_t car = my_car();
    if (car != K.car){ K.car = car; K.dark = 0; }
    int st = lightkey_mine();
    if (st != K.last && lg()) fprintf(stderr, "[lights] f=%ld my lights %s\n", autotest_frame(), st_name(st));
    K.last = st;
    if (guest_ok(car, 0x9e0)){
        if (st == LK_OFF){ MR8(car + CAR_HL_ON) = 0; K.dark = 1; }
        else if (K.dark){ MR8(car + CAR_HL_ON) = 1; K.dark = 0; }    /* (the game's next step sets its own) */
    }
    if (!K.fresh){                                                      /* no free roam this frame: no friends' cars */
        memset(K.fcar, 0, sizeof K.fcar); memset(K.fst, 0, sizeof K.fst); memset(K.fdark, 0, sizeof K.fdark);
    }
    K.fresh = 0;
    for (int k = 0; k < LK_SLOTS; k++){
        uint32_t fc = K.fcar[k];
        if (!fc || !guest_ok(fc, 0x9e0)) continue;
        if (K.fst[k] == LK_OFF){ MR8(fc + CAR_HL_ON) = 0; K.fdark[k] = 1; }
        else if (K.fdark[k]){ MR8(fc + CAR_HL_ON) = 1; K.fdark[k] = 0; }
    }
}

/* ---- the flares ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
 * photo.c's override of 0x615630, around the game's: the car whose flares it draws now (its render info; 0: done) */
void lightkey_flares(uint32_t ri){
    K.flare_ri = ri; K.flare_k = 1.f;
    if (!ri || !guest_ok(ri, 3)) return;
    K.fl_cars++;
    if (lightkey_state(MR32(ri)) == LK_HIGH){ K.flare_k = g_hi_flare; K.fl_cars_hi++; }
}
void sub_00490920_orig(CPU *c);
void sub_00490920(CPU *c){                       /* a light's flare (cdecl: view, light, matrix, strength, ...) */
    if (K.flare_ri && K.flare_k != 1.f){
        uint32_t light = MR32(c->esp + 8u), h = guest_ok(light, 0xb) ? MR32(light + 8u) : 0u;
        if (h == HASH_HL_A || h == HASH_HL_B){ MRF32(c->esp + 0x10u) *= K.flare_k; K.fl_scaled++; }
    }
    if (K.flare_ri){ uint32_t light = MR32(c->esp + 8u), h = guest_ok(light, 0xb) ? MR32(light + 8u) : 0u; K.fl_hl += h == HASH_HL_A || h == HASH_HL_B; }
    sub_00490920_orig(c);
}

/* ---- the road -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- */
float lightkey_hi_gain(void){ return g_hi_gain; }
static int g_noself;                /* test: our high beam as the game's own light, brighter, not aimed higher */
int lightkey_self_ok(void){ return !g_noself; }
float lightkey_hi_pitch(void){ return g_hi_pitch; }
/* headlights.c: whether it lit the road from our car this view render (our high beam, its own light) */
void lightkey_self_lit(int on){ g_self_lit = on; }
/* d3dx_hle.c's SetVector: the game's own light on the road from our car (HEADLIGHTCOLOR) times this */
#define G_SHADER     0x00870910u   /* the shader being drawn with: +0x1C its parameters' handles */
#define SH_HLCOLOR   0x574u        /* ...HEADLIGHTCOLOR's */
uint32_t split_render_player(void);   /* splitscreen.c: the Player* whose view split screen draws now, 0 none */
int lightkey_road_vector(uint32_t handle, uint32_t vec){
    int st = lightkey_mine();
    if (st == LK_NORMAL || guest_rd32(G_FLOW) != 6u) return 0;
    uint32_t rp = split_render_player();
    if (rp && rp != guest_rd32(G_PLAYER1)) return 0;                          /* (another split-screen player's own light) */
    uint32_t sh = guest_rd32(G_SHADER), p = sh ? guest_rd32(sh + 0x1cu) : 0;
    if (!p || !guest_ok(p + SH_HLCOLOR, 3) || MR32(p + SH_HLCOLOR) != handle || !guest_ok(vec, 15)) return 0;
    float k = st == LK_OFF ? 0.f : g_self_lit ? 0.f : g_hi_gain;
    for (uint32_t i = 0; i < 3; i++) MRF32(vec + 4u * i) *= k;
    K.rd_set++;
    return 1;
}

/* the test script's "lights ...": state off|on|high|game (a state of ours, or the game's keys again), hi FLARE GAIN
 * PITCH (high beam's look, for the variants), report */
int lightkey_script(const char *s){
    char w[16] = {0}, a[16] = {0}; float x = 0, y = 0, z = 0;
    int n = sscanf(s, "%15s %15s", w, a);
    if (n < 1) return 0;
    if (!strcasecmp(w, "state") && n == 2){
        K.test = !strcasecmp(a, "off") ? LK_OFF : !strcasecmp(a, "high") ? LK_HIGH : !strcasecmp(a, "on") ? LK_NORMAL : -1;
        return 1;
    }
    if (!strcasecmp(w, "hi") && sscanf(s, "%*s %f %f %f", &x, &y, &z) == 3){ g_hi_flare = x; g_hi_gain = y; g_hi_pitch = z; return 1; }
    if (!strcasecmp(w, "noself") && n == 2){ g_noself = atoi(a) != 0; return 1; }
    if (!strcasecmp(w, "report")){
        fprintf(stderr, "[lights] f=%ld mine %s (off %d, flash %d), taps %lu, holds %lu, car 0x%08x +0x93d %u; high beam: flares x%.2f, road x%.2f, %.1f deg up\n",
                autotest_frame(), st_name(lightkey_mine()), K.off, K.flash, K.taps, K.holds, K.car,
                guest_ok(K.car, 0x9e0) ? MR8(K.car + CAR_HL_ON) : 0u, (double)g_hi_flare, (double)g_hi_gain, (double)g_hi_pitch);
        fprintf(stderr, "[lights]   flares: %lu cars' drawn (%lu on high beam), %lu headlight flares, %lu of them brighter; our road light set %lu times\n",
                K.fl_cars, K.fl_cars_hi, K.fl_hl, K.fl_scaled, K.rd_set);
        for (int k = -1; k < LK_SLOTS; k++){            /* (and the fields 0x615630 draws the headlight flares by) */
            uint32_t c = k < 0 ? K.car : K.fcar[k];
            if (!c || !guest_ok(c, 0x9e0)) continue;
            uint32_t ri = guest_rd32(c + 0x554u), lt = guest_rd32(c + 0x8e4u);
            fprintf(stderr, "[lights]   %s %d car 0x%08x: %s, +0x93d %u, its render info's car 0x%08x, light type %d\n",
                    k < 0 ? "mine" : "slot", k, c, st_name(k < 0 ? lightkey_mine() : K.fst[k]), MR8(c + CAR_HL_ON),
                    ri && guest_ok(ri, 3) ? MR32(ri) : 0u, lt && guest_ok(lt, 4) ? (int)(int8_t)MR8(lt + 4u) : -1);
        }
        return 1;
    }
    return 0;
}

/* lobbyclick.c -- a click on a dialog over the Game Session Lobby is not also
 * a click on the game list under it.
 *
 * The lobby (UI_OLLobbyRoom, package PC_OL_Lobby.fng: Online and LAN; its
 * MessageHandler 0x4fcda0, called only from its vtable 0x795fd0) takes the
 * mouse on message 0x9803f6e2: 0x4faa60 selects the row under the pointer,
 * sorts on a column header or presses a button where the left button went
 * down this frame (0x52d100: the mouse 0x8763d0, updated by 0x5bf860: +0x20
 * buttons swapped, +0x21/+0x22/+0x23 left down / went down / went up, right
 * +0x24.., middle +0x27..).  Its Join (0x49ea80) asks first, online:
 * "Entering a game room may cause you to lose any unread messages ...", whose
 * OK (0x59337816) runs 0x4f1620, which joins the game of the row selected at
 * that moment (0x51f530: by its name).  The dialog takes the press on its OK
 * and closes in that frame, and the lobby got the same press in the same
 * frame: the row under the OK became the selection, and the join went to
 * that row's game and asked for its password if it had one (a player's
 * report, 2026-10-23: "It connects to a different lobby than the one
 * selected. It asks for a password on lobbies that don't have a password").
 * With 11 games or more listed a game's row lies under the OK; the rows under
 * the dialog are dimmed, so the new selection hardly shows.
 * The lobby already keeps the mouse off its list while its other questions
 * are up (+0x1cd: the connection quality question and the password screen,
 * set by 0x4f1620, cleared by their answers 0xbd6234af, 0x8905384,
 * 0xf7f19667); this question never set it.
 *
 * Here: once a dialog is up ([0x838974], seen on the lobby's messages of
 * every frame) the lobby's 0x9803f6e2 runs with +0x1cd set, until no dialog
 * is up and no mouse button is down.  Original: the click on OK also
 * selects the game under it. */
#include "cpu.h"
#include "game.h"

#define FN_LOBBY_MSG  0x004fcda0u   /* thiscall (msg, obj, a3, a4), ret 0x10 */
#define MSG_MOUSE     0x9803f6e2u   /* the lobby's mouse: 0x4faa60, unless +0x1cd */
#define LB_ASKING     0x1cdu        /* byte: one of the lobby's questions is up */
#define G_MOUSE_DOWN  0x008763f1u   /* left button down; right +3, middle +6 */

void sub_004fcda0(CPU *c);
void dispatch_patch(uint32_t a, void (*f)(CPU *));

static int g_dialog;   /* a dialog was up: the lobby's mouse waits for the buttons to go up */

static void lobby_msg(CPU *c){
    uint32_t self = c->ecx;
    if (MR32(G_DLG)) g_dialog = 1;
    else if (!MR8(G_MOUSE_DOWN) && !MR8(G_MOUSE_DOWN + 3u) && !MR8(G_MOUSE_DOWN + 6u)) g_dialog = 0;
    if (MR32(c->esp + 4u) != MSG_MOUSE || !g_dialog || MR8(self + LB_ASKING)){ sub_004fcda0(c); return; }
    MR8(self + LB_ASKING) = 1;
    sub_004fcda0(c);
    MR8(self + LB_ASKING) = 0;
}

void lobbyclick_install(void){ dispatch_patch(FN_LOBBY_MSG, lobby_msg); }

{"id": "AT000547", "source": "archive:A028!/nfsu2-web-public/runtime/look.c", "originalBytes": 16268, "originalSha256": "7c8639d9455654cb28aeac8431af1ee814415eb641d16ca7924aac947e911d73", "originalEncoding": "utf-8", "utf8RangeStart": 0, "utf8RangeEnd": 16268, "utf8TotalBytes": 16268}

/* look.c -- the controller's right stick looks around while driving: the
 * view turns to where the stick points (right looks right, a stick half way
 * out turns half as far) and swings back behind the car once the stick is
 * let go.  Straight back is the game's own Look Back, as the stick's button
 * (NFS Heat's way): the view snaps to the rear and back again.  The PC game
 * has nothing of the kind: only Look Back and the camera's change (the
 * consoles' right stick turned the front end's car viewer only:
 * dinput_pad.c sub_004a5d90).  Everywhere the player drives with the drive
 * camera: free roam, the career's and Quick Race's races, races between
 * players (Online, LAN, free roam's).  Not in photo mode, the replay, a
 * cutscene or the crash and jump slow motion (other camera movers: photo
 * mode's is the developers' debug camera), nor with a screen over the HUD or
 * the game paused: then the view is straight behind again at once.  Where
 * quick chat opens (free roam with others, races between players) the
 * stick's click opens it, and the page keeps the stick from the game while
 * its picker is open (web/src/app/quickchat.ts): the view swings back then.
 * A wheel's and an RC radio's right stick is always at rest
 * (web/src/input/wheel.ts).
 * A stick the game reads is not the look's: with the steering or a pedal on
 * the right stick (the game's Joypad Configuration) the left stick looks
 * round, if the game reads none of it either, else nothing does
 * (dinput_pad.c pad_look_stick; players steered with the right stick, and
 * it turned the view as it steered, 2026-11-03).  The player may turn the
 * look off (the start page's Controls, Site, Free look: settings.ini
 * button_look off): no stick looks round then, the game's camera as it was.
 *
 * How: the drive camera puts the camera where it wants it each frame, in the
 * main loop's update (0x5811C0, before the sound's 0x483B40); the frame is
 * drawn after (0x5CE8A0 .. Present in 0x5D2850).  The camera itself is
 * turned for that: from the main view's setup (overrides.c sub_005c7ec0,
 * view 1, the first of the frame) until after Present (career.c's main-loop
 * hook, the empty call returning to LOOK_END_RET), when its bytes go back as
 * the game made them.  Everything drawn reads the turned one: the views and
 * their culling planes, and the car renderer (0x620AE0), which takes the
 * eye from the view's camera (+0x40) for which of a car's parts it draws
 * (from behind it leaves out the front wheels, looking back the rear ones)
 * and for the car's reflections.  Turning only the view's matrix, as the
 * look did first, drew the cars as seen from behind the car: the wheels on
 * the side looked at missing and the reflections wrong (players' reports,
 * 2026-11-03).  The sound and the drive camera's next frame keep the game's
 * camera; free roam's names and lines over the cars, placed in the HUD's
 * update before the frame is drawn, ask look_eye for the view's eye and
 * direction as drawn (roam_game.c view_eye).  The road's reflection (view
 * 4) turns its own camera the same way, if it has one.
 * The turn: the world about a vertical line (M' = A M, A the turn about the
 * line), which is the camera going round the line the other way, its eye,
 * forward and the point it looks at with it.  The line goes through the
 * car's centre (car +0x60), so a chase camera goes round the car and looks
 * past it; with the eye in or on the car (the bumper and hood cameras:
 * within IN_CAR_M of its centre) it goes through the eye, a turn of the
 * head.  The game's world has z up.  Each frame the turn moves towards the
 * stick's (TAU_S), back at rest the short way round; a stick pointing back
 * (past BACK_RAD either side) keeps to the side it came from.
 * Straight back (within SNAP_IN of it, past SNAP_R out) the stick holds the
 * pad's button bound to Look Back (dinput_pad.c fill_state, look_back_held)
 * and the camera is the game's; it lets go outside SNAP_OUT or below
 * SNAP_R_OFF.  From there to the side the turn goes on from straight back;
 * let go, the view is behind the car at once, as after the button.  With no
 * button bound to Look Back the stick turns the view round to the rear.
 *
 * NFSU2_PAD_LOG=1 logs each look's start and end
 * (tests/scripts/pad_look.txt; roam_look_a.txt in free roam). */
#include "cpu.h"
#include "guest.h"
#include "game.h"
#include "coop.h"
#include "gamepad.h"
#include <math.h>
#include <stdio.h>
#include <stdlib.h>
#include <string.h>
#include <strings.h>
#include <time.h>

#define G_PLAYER1    SPLIT_PLAYERS_INDEX   /* Player*: +4 its car, +0x9A4 its HUD, +0x238 its camera mover */
#define PL_CAR       4u
#define PL_HUD       0x9a4u
#define PL_MOVER     0x238u
#define MV_TYPE      0xcu
#define MOVER_DRIVE  1u
#define CAR_POS      0x60u         /* the car's centre, world */
#define CAM_POS      0x40u         /* the camera's eye, world */
#define CAM_FWD      0x50u         /*   its forward */
#define CAM_TARGET   0x60u         /*   the point it looks at */
#define CAM_TURNED   0x70u         /* its bytes the turn changes: the matrix, those three */
#define NCAM         2             /* the cameras turned in a frame: view 1's, view 4's if its own */

#define STICK_ON     0.25f         /* the stick starts a look past this far out (after the dead zone) */
#define STICK_FULL   0.85f         /* and turns the whole way from this far */
#define TAU_S        0.09f         /* the turn's time constant towards the stick's */
#define BACK_RAD     2.4f          /* a stick pointing back past this (rad, ~137 degrees) keeps the turn's side */
#define SNAP_IN      0.44f         /* within this of straight back (rad, ~25 degrees) the stick holds Look Back, */
#define SNAP_OUT     0.61f         /*   and lets go outside this (~35 degrees), */
#define SNAP_R       0.5f          /*   from this far out, */
#define SNAP_R_OFF   0.4f          /*   down to this */
#define IN_CAR_M     3.f           /* the eye this near the car's centre (m, flat): the bumper and hood cameras */
#define REST_RAD     0.0005f       /* a turn this small is none */
#define PI_F         3.14159265f

long autotest_frame(void);         /* autotest.c: the game's Present count */

static struct {
    float yaw;                     /* the turn now, rad (+ looks right) */
    float px, py;                  /* the line it turns about, this frame */
    int on;                        /* turned this frame (views 1 and 4) */
    int looking;                   /* the stick out (for the log) */
    int back;                      /* the stick straight back: it holds Look Back */
    double t;                      /* the last frame's clock */
    int n;                         /* the cameras turned now (until look_frame_end), in Present count frame */
    long frame;
    uint32_t cam[NCAM];
    uint8_t keep[NCAM][CAM_TURNED];    /* their bytes as the game made them */
    uint8_t made[NCAM][CAM_TURNED];    /* and as turned */
} L;

static double now_s(void){ struct timespec ts; clock_gettime(CLOCK_MONOTONIC, &ts); return ts.tv_sec + ts.tv_nsec * 1e-9; }
static float wrap(float a){
    while (a > PI_F) a -= 2.f * PI_F;
    while (a < -PI_F) a += 2.f * PI_F;
    return a;
}
static int pad_log(void){
    static int l = -1;
    if (l < 0) l = gamepad_env_flag("NFSU2_PAD_LOG", 0);
    return l;
}

/* the player's car while it drives with the drive camera and the HUD on top (0: no look now) */
static uint32_t driving_car(void){
    uint32_t pl = guest_rd32(G_PLAYER1), r = guest_rd32(G_RACE);
    if (MR32(G_FLOW) != 6u || !guest_ok(pl, PL_MOVER + 4u) || !guest_ok(r, 3) || MR32(r) != 4u) return 0;
    uint32_t car = guest_rd32(pl + PL_CAR), mv = guest_rd32(pl + PL_MOVER);
    if (!guest_ok(car, CAR_POS + 12u) || !guest_ok(mv, MV_TYPE + 4u) || MR32(mv + MV_TYPE) != MOVER_DRIVE) return 0;
    uint32_t hud = guest_rd32(pl + PL_HUD), fe = guest_rd32(G_FENG), mg = fe ? guest_rd32(fe + 8u) : 0, top = mg ? coop_fe_top(mg) : 0;
    char a[40], b[40];
    guest_read_str(top ? guest_rd32(top + 0xcu) : 0, a, sizeof a); guest_read_str(hud ? guest_rd32(hud + 0x10u) : 0, b, sizeof b);
    return a[0] && !strcasecmp(a, b) ? car : 0;
}

/* how far the stick at x, y points from straight back (rad, 0 .. pi) */
static float from_back(float x, float y){ return PI_F - fabsf(atan2f(x, -y)); }

/* the turn the stick asks for now (rad, + right; 0 at rest), its back side kept as the turn now has it; *back: it
 * points straight back, where it holds Look Back (where a button has it) instead of turning the view */
int pad_look_stick(void);                            /* dinput_pad.c: PAD_AXIS_RX, PAD_AXIS_LX (Y the next), -1 none */
static float stick_yaw(int can, int *back){
    PadState s;
    *back = 0;
    int st = pad_look_stick();
    if (!can || st < 0 || !gamepad_read(&s) || s.wheel) return 0.f;
    float x = s.axis[st], y = s.axis[st + 1], r = hypotf(x, y);
    int pad_look_back_bound(void);                   /* dinput_pad.c: a button of the pad's is Look Back */
    if (pad_look_back_bound()){
        float off = from_back(x, y);
        if (L.back ? off < SNAP_OUT && r > SNAP_R_OFF : off < SNAP_IN && r > SNAP_R){ *back = 1; return 0.f; }
        if (off < (L.back ? SNAP_OUT : SNAP_IN)) return 0.f;   /* on its way out there or back in: no turn */
    }
    if (r < STICK_ON) return 0.f;
    float k = fminf(1.f, (r - STICK_ON) / (STICK_FULL - STICK_ON));
    float dir = atan2f(x, -y);                       /* up 0, right +pi/2, down pi, left -pi/2 */
    int side = fabsf(L.yaw) > 0.05f ? (L.yaw > 0.f ? 1 : -1) : (x >= 0.f ? 1 : -1);
    if (fabsf(dir) > BACK_RAD && (dir > 0.f ? 1 : -1) != side) dir += side * 2.f * PI_F;
    return dir * k;
}

/* dinput_pad.c fill_state, as the game reads the pad: whether the stick (in s) holds the button bound to Look Back */
int look_back_held(const PadState *s){
    int st = pad_look_stick();
    if (!L.back || !s || s->wheel || st < 0) return 0;
    float x = s->axis[st], y = s->axis[st + 1];
    return hypotf(x, y) > SNAP_R_OFF && from_back(x, y) < SNAP_OUT && driving_car() != 0;
}

/* p (a point, or a direction with pt 0) turned as the view is: clockwise seen from above about the line */
static void turn_xy(float *p, int pt){
    float c = cosf(L.yaw), s = sinf(L.yaw), ox = pt ? L.px : 0.f, oy = pt ? L.py : 0.f, x = p[0] - ox, y = p[1] - oy;
    p[0] = ox + x * c + y * s; p[1] = oy - x * s + y * c;
}

/* the camera's matrix at cam (rows; the translation in the last; points as rows times it) turned: the world turned
 * about the line first, anticlockwise seen from above by the look's angle, so the camera goes round it clockwise and
 * looks right (the game's world: x, y, z up as a right hand has them) */
static void turn_matrix(uint32_t cam){
    float c = cosf(L.yaw), s = -sinf(L.yaw), *M = (float *)(g_mem + cam);
    /* A: rows (c, -s, 0), (s, c, 0), (0, 0, 1) (the world by -s's angle, anticlockwise), translation p - p R */
    float tx = L.px - (L.px * c + L.py * s), ty = L.py - (-L.px * s + L.py * c);
    float r0[4], r1[4];
    for (int k = 0; k < 4; k++){
        r0[k] = c * M[k] - s * M[4 + k];
        r1[k] = s * M[k] + c * M[4 + k];
    }
    for (int k = 0; k < 4; k++){
        M[12 + k] += tx * M[k] + ty * M[4 + k];
        M[k] = r0[k]; M[4 + k] = r1[k];
    }
}

/* the camera at cam turned for the rest of the frame (once), its bytes kept for look_frame_end */
static void turn_camera(uint32_t cam){
    if (!guest_ok(cam, CAM_TURNED) || L.n >= NCAM) return;
    for (int i = 0; i < L.n; i++) if (L.cam[i] == cam) return;
    memcpy(L.keep[L.n], g_mem + cam, CAM_TURNED);
    turn_matrix(cam);
    turn_xy((float *)(g_mem + cam + CAM_POS), 1);
    turn_xy((float *)(g_mem + cam + CAM_FWD), 0);
    turn_xy((float *)(g_mem + cam + CAM_TARGET), 1);
    memcpy(L.made[L.n], g_mem + cam, CAM_TURNED);
    L.cam[L.n++] = cam;
    L.frame = autotest_frame();
}

/* career.c's main-loop hook after Present: the cameras back as the game made them (unless something wrote them since) */
void look_frame_end(void){
    for (int i = 0; i < L.n; i++){
        uint32_t cam = L.cam[i];
        if (!guest_ok(cam, CAM_TURNED)) continue;
        if (!memcmp(g_mem + cam, L.made[i], CAM_TURNED)) memcpy(g_mem + cam, L.keep[i], CAM_TURNED);
        else if (pad_log()) fprintf(stderr, "[pad] the look's camera 0x%08x was written while turned: left as it is\n", cam);
    }
    L.n = 0;
}

/* overrides.c sub_005c7ec0, before the view is made, for views 1 (the main view: once a frame, first) and 4 (its road
 * reflection) and their cameras: the camera turned now for the frame, as the stick asks */
void look_view(uint32_t id, uint32_t cam){
    if (id != 1u){
        static int said;
        if (pad_log() && L.on && !said){
            said = 1;
            fprintf(stderr, "[pad] look: view %u's camera 0x%08x, %s\n", id, cam, L.n && L.cam[0] == cam ? "view 1's" : "its own");
        }
        if (L.on) turn_camera(cam);                  /* a camera of its own (view 1's is turned already) */
        return;
    }
    for (int i = 0; i < L.n; i++) if (L.cam[i] == cam) return;   /* made again this frame: turned already */
    if (L.n && L.frame != autotest_frame()) look_frame_end();    /* a frame that ended without the hook */
    double t = now_s();
    float dt = L.t > 0. ? (float)(t - L.t) : 0.f;
    L.t = t;
    if (dt > 0.25f) dt = 0.25f;
    uint32_t car = driving_car();
    int back = 0;
    float want = stick_yaw(car != 0, &back);
    const char *which = pad_look_stick() == PAD_AXIS_LX ? "left" : "right";
    if (pad_log() && back != L.back)
        fprintf(stderr, back ? "[pad] the %s stick holds Look Back\n" : "[pad] the %s stick lets go of Look Back\n", which);
    if (pad_log() && !back && !L.back && (want != 0.f) != L.looking){
        if (want != 0.f) fprintf(stderr, "[pad] the %s stick looks round the car\n", which);
        else fprintf(stderr, "[pad] the %s stick let go (the view turned %.0f degrees)%s\n", which,
                     (double)(L.yaw * 57.29578f), car ? "" : ": no look now");
    }
    L.looking = want != 0.f;
    if (back){                                       /* the game's own view to the rear: the turn waits there */
        if (!L.back) L.yaw = L.yaw < -0.05f ? -PI_F : PI_F;
        L.back = 1;
        L.on = 0;
        return;
    }
    if (L.back){
        L.back = 0;
        if (want == 0.f) L.yaw = 0.f;                /* let go from straight back: behind the car at once */
    }
    float d = want - L.yaw;
    if (d > PI_F) d -= 2.f * PI_F; else if (d < -PI_F) d += 2.f * PI_F;
    L.yaw = wrap(L.yaw + d * (1.f - expf(-dt / TAU_S)));
    if (!car || (want == 0.f && fabsf(L.yaw) < REST_RAD)){
        if (!car) L.yaw = 0.f;                       /* no look now: straight behind at once (a screen, a replay) */
        else if (fabsf(L.yaw) < REST_RAD) L.yaw = 0.f;
        L.on = 0;
        return;
    }
    float cx = MRF32(car + CAR_POS), cy = MRF32(car + CAR_POS + 4u);
    if (guest_ok(cam, CAM_POS + 12u)){
        float ex = MRF32(cam + CAM_POS), ey = MRF32(cam + CAM_POS + 4u);
        if (hypotf(ex - cx, ey - cy) < IN_CAR_M){ cx = ex; cy = ey; }
    }
    L.px = cx; L.py = cy;
    L.on = 1;
    turn_camera(cam);
    static int said;
    if (pad_log() && !said && L.n){
        const float *k = (const float *)L.keep[0];
        said = 1;
        fprintf(stderr, "[pad] look: camera 0x%08x eye (%.2f %.2f %.2f) forward (%.3f %.3f %.3f) +0x60 (%.2f %.2f %.2f)"
                " car (%.2f %.2f %.2f)\n", cam, (double)k[16], (double)k[17], (double)k[18], (double)k[20],
                (double)k[21], (double)k[22], (double)k[24], (double)k[25], (double)k[26], (double)MRF32(car + CAR_POS),
                (double)MRF32(car + CAR_POS + 4u), (double)MRF32(car + CAR_POS + 8u));
    }
}

/* the main view's eye and forward e, f (the camera's, as read while it is not turned: the HUD's update) turned as the
 * frame is drawn: what the view looks from and along (roam_game.c's names over the cars and lines over them: what is
 * in front) */
void look_eye(float *e, float *f){
    if (!L.on || L.n) return;                        /* turned now: the camera says so itself */
    turn_xy(e, 1);
    turn_xy(f, 0);
}

/* the runtime heap's break (runtime/web/sbrk.c; none in a test program that has libc's own) */
__attribute__((weak)) uint64_t heap_break(void);

/* The guest heap's window: on, once, where the page asked for it
 * (NFSU2_HEAP_WINDOW=1, a computer's browser: host/process.ts) and the memory
 * it gave reaches the window's top, with the runtime's heap still below the
 * window.  Phones, tablets and Safari get no window and today's layout.
 * NFSU2_HEAP_WINDOW=0 turns it off where the page would ask.  The line says
 * which. */
void mem_window_init(void){
    static int done = 0;
    if (done) return;
    done = 1;
    const char *e = getenv("NFSU2_HEAP_WINDOW");
    if (!e || strcmp(e, "1")) return;
    uint64_t have = (uint64_t)__builtin_wasm_memory_size(0) * 65536u, brk = heap_break ? heap_break() : 0;
    if (have < GWIN_HI || brk > GWIN_LO){
        fprintf(stderr, "[heap] no window above the runtime: the memory is %llu MB (%u MB wanted), the runtime's heap at %llu MB\n",
                (unsigned long long)(have >> 20), (GWIN_HI + 0xFFFFFu) >> 20, (unsigned long long)(brk >> 20));
        return;
    }
    __atomic_store_n(&g_gwin_lo, GWIN_LO, __ATOMIC_RELEASE);
    __atomic_store_n(&g_gwin_hi, GWIN_HI, __ATOMIC_RELEASE);
    fprintf(stderr, "[heap] window above the runtime: 0x%08x..0x%08x (%u MB more guest heap; memory %llu MB, the runtime's heap at %llu MB)\n",
            GWIN_LO, GWIN_HI, (GWIN_HI - GWIN_LO + 0xFFFFFu) >> 20, (unsigned long long)(have >> 20), (unsigned long long)(brk >> 20));
    /* NFSU2_TEST_HIGH_RUNTIME=1 (test runs: with NFSU2_INPUT_SCRIPT): the runtime's heap past the window from its next
     * growth on, at 2 GB or more, as after a long session (sbrk.c) */
    const char *hr = getenv("NFSU2_TEST_HIGH_RUNTIME"), *scr = getenv("NFSU2_INPUT_SCRIPT");
    if (&g_sbrk_high && hr && !strcmp(hr, "1") && scr && *scr){
        g_sbrk_high = 1;
        fprintf(stderr, "[heap] NFSU2_TEST_HIGH_RUNTIME: the runtime's heap goes on past the window, at 2 GB or more\n");
    }
}
/* [lo, hi) cut to one of the guest's spans ([0, GUEST_END) or the window): 0 when it is in neither */
static int guest_cut(uint64_t *lo, uint64_t *hi){
    if (*lo < GUEST_END){ if (*hi > GUEST_END) *hi = GUEST_END; return 1; }
    if (g_gwin_hi && *lo >= g_gwin_lo && *lo < g_gwin_hi){ if (*hi > g_gwin_hi) *hi = g_gwin_hi; return 1; }
    return 0;
}
void mem_commit(uint32_t addr, uint32_t size){
    uint64_t lo = addr & ~0x3FFFull;
    uint64_t hi = ((uint64_t)addr + size + 0x3FFF) & ~0x3FFFull, want = hi;
    int in = guest_cut(&lo, &hi);
    if (!in || hi < want){
        static int shown = 0;
        if (shown++ < 8) fprintf(stderr, "mem_commit 0x%08x+%u beyond the guest span (0x%08x%s): ignored\n", addr, size, GUEST_END,
                                 g_gwin_hi ? " and the window" : "");
        if (!in) return;
    }
    for (uint64_t a2 = lo; a2 < hi; a2 += 0x4000ull){
        uint32_t pg = (uint32_t)(a2 >> 14);
        if (!(g_cbits[pg>>3] & (1u << (pg&7)))){ g_cbits[pg>>3] |= (uint8_t)(1u << (pg&7)); g_committed += 0x4000u; }
    }
}
uint64_t mem_committed(void){ return g_committed; }
void mem_release(uint32_t addr, uint32_t size, int rw){
    uint64_t lo = ((uint64_t)addr + 0x3FFF) & ~0x3FFFull;
    uint64_t hi = ((uint64_t)addr + size) & ~0x3FFFull, want = hi;
    if (hi <= lo || !guest_cut(&lo, &hi) || hi < want) return;
    memset(g_mem + lo, rw ? 0 : 0xDD, (size_t)(hi - lo));     /* rw=0 (HEAPCHECK): poison, no fault */
    for (uint64_t a2 = lo; a2 < hi; a2 += 0x4000ull){
        uint32_t pg = (uint32_t)(a2 >> 14);
        if (rw) g_cbits[pg>>3] |= (uint8_t)(1u << (pg&7));
        else    g_cbits[pg>>3] &= (uint8_t)~(1u << (pg&7));
    }
}

void mem_init(void){
    if (g_mem) return;
    g_mem = mmap(0, GSZ, PROT_NONE, MAP_PRIVATE|MAP_ANON|MAP_NORESERVE, -1, 0);
    if (g_mem == MAP_FAILED){ perror("mmap 4GB"); exit(1); }
}

void mem_commit(uint32_t addr, uint32_t size){
    uint64_t lo = addr & ~0x3FFFull;                    /* 16 KB page */
    uint64_t hi = ((uint64_t)addr + size + 0x3FFF) & ~0x3FFFull;
    if (hi > 0x100000000ull) hi = 0x100000000ull;
    if (mprotect(g_mem + lo, hi - lo, PROT_READ|PROT_WRITE) != 0){
        fprintf(stderr,"mem_commit 0x%08x+%u failed\n", addr, size); exit(1);
    }
    for (uint64_t a2 = lo; a2 < hi; a2 += 0x4000ull){
        uint32_t pg = (uint32_t)(a2 >> 14);
        g_cbits[pg>>3] |= (uint8_t)(1u << (pg&7));
    }
    g_committed += hi - lo;
    /* WATCHADDR=<address>: arm the watchpoint as soon as that address is
     * committed, so even the first writer is caught. */
    { static int wa_done = 0;
      const char *wa = getenv("WATCHADDR");
      if (wa && !wa_done){
          uint32_t t = (uint32_t)strtoul(wa, 0, 0);
          if ((uint64_t)t >= lo && (uint64_t)t < hi){ wa_done = 1; mprot_arm(t); }
      } }
}
uint64_t mem_committed(void){ return g_committed; }

/* Guest heap (heap.c): give a released range back to the host.  The range is
 * replaced by fresh anonymous pages, so its physical memory is freed at once
 * and it reads as zero afterwards.  rw=1 keeps it accessible (a stale guest
 * pointer then reads zeros, as it read old data under the bump allocator);
 * rw=0 makes it PROT_NONE so a use-after-release faults (NFSU2_HEAPCHECK).
 * Only whole 16 KB host pages inside [addr, addr+size) are touched. */
void mem_release(uint32_t addr, uint32_t size, int rw){
    uint64_t lo = ((uint64_t)addr + 0x3FFF) & ~0x3FFFull;
    uint64_t hi = ((uint64_t)addr + size) & ~0x3FFFull;
    if (hi <= lo) return;
    void *p = mmap(g_mem + lo, hi - lo, rw ? (PROT_READ|PROT_WRITE) : PROT_NONE,
                   MAP_FIXED|MAP_PRIVATE|MAP_ANON|MAP_NORESERVE, -1, 0);
    if (p == MAP_FAILED){ fprintf(stderr,"mem_release 0x%08x+%u failed (%s)\n", addr, size, strerror(errno)); return; }
    for (uint64_t a2 = lo; a2 < hi; a2 += 0x4000ull){
        uint32_t pg = (uint32_t)(a2 >> 14);
        if (rw) g_cbits[pg>>3] |= (uint8_t)(1u << (pg&7));
        else    g_cbits[pg>>3] &= (uint8_t)~(1u << (pg&7));
    }
}

/* Diagnose a guest access to an uncommitted region */
static volatile int g_in_handler = 0;
/* --- write capture: make a guest page read-only and find the writer ---
 * Answers "who writes this memory?" without watchpoint instrumentation:
 * the write raises SIGSEGV, and the generated function (hence the guest
 * function) is resolved from the faulting host PC.                       */
uint8_t *g_mprot_page = 0;
static size_t g_mprot_sz = 0;
static int g_mprot_hits = 0;
static uint32_t g_mprot_target = 0;      /* the exact address we care about */
static volatile int g_mprot_found = 0;   /* the target's writer was found */
static int      g_mprot_persist = 0;     /* re-arm every frame */
/* provided by dispatch.c; weak default for standalone-linked test runs */
__attribute__((weak)) uint32_t guest_fn_from_host(const void *pc){ (void)pc; return 0; }

/* The protected page is 16 KB and very busy: the first unrelated write drops
 * the protection.  A separate thread keeps re-arming it, so the target's
 * writer gets caught. */
static void *mprot_rearm_thread(void *a0){
    (void)a0;
    for (;;){
        /* re-protect even when g_mprot_page is set: an intervening
         * mem_commit may have silently removed the protection. */
        if (g_mprot_target && !g_mprot_found){
            size_t ps = (size_t)getpagesize();
            uint8_t *pg = (uint8_t*)((uintptr_t)(g_mem + g_mprot_target) & ~(uintptr_t)(ps-1));
            if (mprotect(pg, ps, PROT_READ) == 0){ g_mprot_page = pg; g_mprot_sz = ps; }
        }
        struct timespec ts = {0, 50 * 1000};    /* 50 us */
        nanosleep(&ts, 0);
    }
    return 0;
}

void mprot_arm(uint32_t guest_addr){
    /* On Apple Silicon a page is 16 KB; take the alignment from the system value. */
    size_t ps = (size_t)getpagesize();
    uint8_t *pg = (uint8_t*)((uintptr_t)(g_mem + guest_addr) & ~(uintptr_t)(ps - 1));
    if (mprotect(pg, ps, PROT_READ) != 0){
        fprintf(stderr,"mprot: could not be set up (%s)\n", strerror(errno)); return;
    }
    g_mprot_page = pg; g_mprot_sz = ps; g_mprot_target = guest_addr;
    g_mprot_persist = getenv("MPROT_PERSIST") ? 1 : 0;
    if (getenv("MPROT_HARD")){
        static pthread_t th; static int started = 0;
        if (!started){ started = 1; pthread_create(&th, 0, mprot_rearm_thread, 0); }
    }
    fprintf(stderr,"mprot: guest 0x%08x page read-only (to catch the writer)\n",
            guest_addr);
}

/* Re-arm the protection at the start of a frame (when one capture is not enough). */
void mprot_rearm(void){
    if (!g_mprot_persist || g_mprot_page || !g_mprot_target) return;
    size_t ps = (size_t)getpagesize();
    uint8_t *pg = (uint8_t*)((uintptr_t)(g_mem + g_mprot_target) & ~(uintptr_t)(ps - 1));
    if (mprotect(pg, ps, PROT_READ) == 0){ g_mprot_page = pg; g_mprot_sz = ps; }
}

static void segv(int sig, siginfo_t *si, void *uc){
    (void)sig;
    /* a write to the protected page? */
    if (g_mprot_page){
        uint8_t *fa = (uint8_t*)si->si_addr;
        if (fa >= g_mprot_page && fa < g_mprot_page + g_mprot_sz){
            void *pc = 0;
#if defined(__aarch64__)
            ucontext_t *u = (ucontext_t*)uc;
            if (u && u->uc_mcontext) pc = (void*)(uintptr_t)u->uc_mcontext->__ss.__pc;
#endif
            uint32_t gfn = pc ? guest_fn_from_host(pc) : 0;
            uint32_t ga = (uint32_t)(fa - g_mem);
            int interesting = !g_mprot_target ||
                (ga >= g_mprot_target && ga < g_mprot_target + 64u);
            if (getenv("MPROT_ANY")) interesting = 1;   /* mechanism test */
            if (interesting && g_mprot_hits < 12){
                g_mprot_hits++;
                fprintf(stderr,"mprot: WRITE TO TARGET guest 0x%08x  guest function=sub_%08x\n",
                        ga, gfn);
                if (g_mprot_hits >= 6) g_mprot_found = 1;
            }
            mprotect(g_mprot_page, g_mprot_sz, PROT_READ|PROT_WRITE);
            g_mprot_page = 0;           /* one-shot */
            return;                      /* let the instruction run again */
        }
    }
    if (g_in_handler){ fprintf(stderr,"\n*** a second fault inside the handler - exiting\n"); _exit(4); }
    g_in_handler = 1;
    /* The GUEST FUNCTION that faulted: resolved from the host PC.  The stack
     * trace only gives the callers; this tells exactly where the fault was. */
    { void *fpc = 0;
#if defined(__aarch64__)
      ucontext_t *u2 = (ucontext_t*)uc;
      if (u2 && u2->uc_mcontext) fpc = (void*)(uintptr_t)u2->uc_mcontext->__ss.__pc;
#endif
      uint32_t ffn = fpc ? guest_fn_from_host(fpc) : 0;
      if (ffn) fprintf(stderr,"\n*** FAULT IN GUEST FUNCTION: sub_%08x\n", ffn);
    }
    uint8_t *p = (uint8_t*)si->si_addr;
    if (p >= g_mem && p < g_mem + GSZ)
        fprintf(stderr,"\n*** GUEST MEMORY FAULT: guest address 0x%08llx (unmapped)\n",
                (unsigned long long)(p - g_mem));
    else
        fprintf(stderr,"\n*** HOST SEGV: %p (outside the guest area - probably a HOST STACK OVERFLOW:"
                       " endless recursion in guest code)\n", p);
    { extern uint32_t g_watch_prev_ip; extern uint64_t g_itrace_n;
      if (g_itrace_n) fprintf(stderr,"    GUEST INSTRUCTION THAT FAULTED: 0x%08x\n", g_watch_prev_ip); }
    if (g_cur_cpu){
        CPU *c = (CPU*)g_cur_cpu;
        fprintf(stderr,"    eax=%08x ecx=%08x edx=%08x ebx=%08x\n", c->eax,c->ecx,c->edx,c->ebx);
        fprintf(stderr,"    esp=%08x ebp=%08x esi=%08x edi=%08x  df=%u\n", c->esp,c->ebp,c->esi,c->edi,c->df);
        fprintf(stderr,"    fs_base=%08x tid=%u   [ebp+8]=%08x [ebp+4]=%08x\n",
                c->fs_base,
                (c->fs_base && mem_is_committed(c->fs_base+0x24u)) ? MR32(c->fs_base+0x24u) : 0u,
                mem_is_committed(c->ebp+8u) ? MR32(c->ebp+8u) : 0xDEADu,
                mem_is_committed(c->ebp+4u) ? MR32(c->ebp+4u) : 0xDEADu);
    }
    if (g_cur_cpu && g_backtrace_fn) g_backtrace_fn(g_cur_cpu, 12);
    if (g_itrace_dump_fn && getenv("ITRACE")) g_itrace_dump_fn(atoi(getenv("ITRACE")));
    if (g_report_fn) g_report_fn();
    _exit(3);
}
/* sigaltstack is set up PER THREAD: every guest thread must set up its own
 * signal stack, or on a stack overflow the handler crashes too.        */
void mem_altstack_install(void){
    size_t sz = (size_t)SIGSTKSZ * 8;
    void *p = malloc(sz);
    if (!p) return;
    stack_t ss; ss.ss_sp = p; ss.ss_size = sz; ss.ss_flags = 0;
    sigaltstack(&ss, 0);
}
void mem_fault_handler_install(void){
    mem_altstack_install();
    struct sigaction sa; memset(&sa,0,sizeof sa);
    sa.sa_sigaction = segv; sa.sa_flags = SA_SIGINFO | SA_ONSTACK;
    sigaction(SIGSEGV,&sa,0); sigaction(SIGBUS,&sa,0);
}

#endif /* !__wasm__ */

int mem_load_pe(const char *path){
    FILE *f = fopen(path, "rb");
    if(!f){ perror(path); return -1; }
    fseek(f,0,SEEK_END); long sz=ftell(f); fseek(f,0,SEEK_SET);
    uint8_t *buf = malloc(sz);
    if (fread(buf,1,sz,f)!=(size_t)sz){ fclose(f); free(buf); return -1; }
    fclose(f);
    uint32_t e_lfanew = *(uint32_t*)(buf+0x3c);
    uint8_t *nt = buf + e_lfanew;
    if (*(uint32_t*)nt != 0x00004550u){ fprintf(stderr,"no PE signature\n"); free(buf); return -1; }
    uint16_t nsec  = *(uint16_t*)(nt+6);
    uint16_t optsz = *(uint16_t*)(nt+20);
    uint32_t base  = *(uint32_t*)(nt+24+28);
    uint32_t imgsz = *(uint32_t*)(nt+24+56);
    /* DataDirectory[2] = RESOURCE */
    { /* PE32: DataDirectory at byte 96 of the optional header; RESOURCE = index 2 */
      uint32_t dd = 24 + 96 + 2*8;
      uint32_t rva = *(uint32_t*)(nt + dd);
      uint32_t sz  = *(uint32_t*)(nt + dd + 4);
      g_image_base = base; g_res_dir_va = rva ? base + rva : 0; g_res_dir_size = sz; }
    uint8_t *sh    = nt + 24 + optsz;
    mem_init();
    mem_commit(base, imgsz);                 /* the whole image range */
    for (int i=0;i<nsec;i++){
        uint8_t *s = sh + i*40;
        char nm[9]={0}; memcpy(nm,s,8);
        uint32_t vsize=*(uint32_t*)(s+8), va=*(uint32_t*)(s+12);
        uint32_t rsize=*(uint32_t*)(s+16), roff=*(uint32_t*)(s+20);
        uint32_t n = rsize < vsize ? rsize : vsize;
        memcpy(g_mem + base + va, buf + roff, n);
        fprintf(stderr,"  loaded %-9s -> 0x%08x  %u bytes\n", nm[0]?nm:"<unnamed>", base+va, n);
    }
    free(buf);
    fprintf(stderr,"  image 0x%08x .. 0x%08x   resource directory 0x%08x (%u bytes)\n",
            base, base+imgsz, g_res_dir_va, g_res_dir_size);
    return 0;
}
